claims.finding: The September-2025 template has been repeated but unbundled: on 2025-09-03 YQ announced a $10m repurchase and printed Q2 results on 2025-09-04, and the baseline records that combined event as +19.02%; in 2026 the identical $10m repurchase was approved effective 2026-09-03 but the results 6-K is six sessions later, and the buyback leg alone has already produced +21.5% on 2026-09-03 and +93.4% over five sessions, taking the market cap from the $24.75m recorded in event.json to roughly $41m at the 2026-09-08 close of 3.79 against the ~$51m of cash the buyback release was being read against.

claims.why_not_priced: The company has no consensus at all (event.json n_estimates N/A, consensus null), no analyst coverage, and a 7.51m-share float on ~$17k of normal daily liquidity, so nothing about the print itself is in a model anywhere. What is priced, violently, is the buyback and the cash-shell discount: the discount to net cash has gone from about 51% on 2026-09-03 to about 20% by 2026-09-08, so the specific valuation argument that was being posted as the reason to buy is roughly 60% consumed before the results even arrive. If the print itself were the driver, the volume spike would be sitting on 2026-09-09 rather than on 2026-09-03.
claims.independence: Shares a source document with finding 3, declared. Corroborated from a different file: the baseline's own session_conflict block for 2026-09-03 shows event_day_volume 2,789,500 against a median_20d_before of 4,600 - a 600x volume event six sessions before the print - and filings.json confirms the 2026-09-03 6-K (accession 0001193125-26-380968) is a separate filing from the 2026-09-09 results 6-K, so the two catalysts are genuinely distinct events this year.

claims.why_not_priced: The baseline's history block is explicitly discounted (history_usable 0, tier thin, verdict suspect) because the event date does not fit the filing cadence, so the one statistic that actually matters here - that a triple-digit revenue growth print produced -4.58% at a lower price and with no run-up - is being thrown away rather than used. Separating the three real results 6-Ks (2025-09-04 +19.02%, 2026-03-25 0.0%, 2026-06-17 -4.58%) from the five non-results 6-Ks the text matcher caught is work nobody does, and it says the only up-print in the sample was the one paired with a buyback. Marked body_available false because the 6-K text itself is not stored; the growth figure reaches me only through two social bodies.

claims.finding: The 'CEO is buying' stream that ran alongside the squeeze is twelve open-market purchases between 2026-07-20 and 2026-09-04 that together take Liu Chang from 35,149 to 113,070 shares - about 78,000 shares for roughly $170,000, i.e. under 0.7% of the market cap and about 1% of the 7.51m float, in individual tickets of $2,079 to $23,788 - and it stopped on 2026-09-04.
claims.corpus_ref: filings.json - twelve Form 4 accessions dated 2026-07-06, 07-20, 07-22, 07-31, 08-03, 08-10, 08-11, 08-14, 08-24, 08-28, 09-01, 09-03, 09-04; per-transaction sizes and the running holding from the twelve timestamped ceo-buys.com messages in docs/c64c6b6862121be1edca7d02c3f510e6f2384e9a.txt
claims.why_not_priced: Each individual Form 4 generated its own bullish headline - twelve of them, all tagged Bullish on the social feed, one roughly every five sessions - so the market has received twelve separate insider-buying signals and no aggregate. Totalled, it is a sub-$200k drip that is immaterial to a $25-41m company and is roughly the size of two normal days of dollar volume; the drumbeat was a headline generator, not a stake build. Nobody sums a Form 4 series, which is exactly why the corpus contains the twelve announcements and no total.
